audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Neeko Levels 1-2 outright and split Level 3 and Level 6, while both the packet chart and the already-audited mirror have Garen owning Levels 1 through 6. Row 6 also disagreed between layers: phases[6].side said Skill, win[6] said Neeko.
audit.why: garen__neeko sets Garen 7/10, Garen 7/10, Garen 6/10, Garen 6.5/10, Garen 6/10, Skill 5/10 for rows 0-5, and the packet chart agrees. My side must state the same result inverted. The whys already written on my page (Q silence beats my cast, I only last-hit at range) describe a losing early, so the sides were contradicting my own text.
audit.corrected: Rows 0,1,2,4 -> Garen; row 5 -> Skill; row 6 layer disagreement resolved to Neeko in both layers. Ratings inverted from the mirror. Proposed as one atomic group with every full/content pair together.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was sold as 'genuinely even', and both mid and wants.you[1] told the player to channel the ult 'invisible off W'.
audit.why: Neeko's W is a third-attack proc plus a directional clone in Riot's text — no invisibility, no stealth flag. The concealment that actually exists is Inherent Glamour hiding the Pop Blossom preparation. Level 6 also sits behind Courage's tenacity and Demacian Justice, so it is not even.
audit.corrected: whys[4] rewritten to Garen's side with the real reasons; mid and wants.you[1] now use the disguise and the clone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Decisive Strike's auto-attack reset was never named as the burst tell, and Courage's cooldown never appeared anywhere.
audit.why: _missing flags autoreset-burst-tell and shield-absorbs-burst for this matchup. Courage is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s and Decisive Strike is a flat 8s with a silence — those two numbers are the whole step-up decision.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns and the auto-reset tell written into report[5].t, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[0].d.

audit.why: The page's treatment of Demacian Justice as missing-HP true damage matches the kit's trueDamage and execute flags, so resistances genuinely do not answer it. Kept as written.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it' gave no number for the cooldown the whole matchup is scheduled around.
audit.why: Concrete timers make the advice usable; 22s at rank 1 is a long window, 12s at rank 5 is not, and that difference changes how the lane is played.

edits.before: Level 6 is genuinely even — my landed E into Pop Blossom stun is a real all-in, but his W tenacity and missing-HP true-damage R can flip it, so it comes down to execution.
edits.after: Level 6 narrows it but stays his — a landed E into Pop Blossom is a real all-in, yet Courage's tenacity cuts the stun short and Demacian Justice executes straight through my MR.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay his — I shove with Q waveclear and poke, but I will not all-in a Garen who can W away the burst and silence my follow-up. Level 6 is where I get even footing: if I land E and chain Pop Blossom's stun, that is a real kill threat, and I can channel the ult while disguised or invisible off W so he never sees it coming. The catch is honest — his W gives tenacity that shortens my stun, and his missing-HP true-damage R can out-trade me if my combo doesn't kill outright. Bait the Q, bait the W, then commit.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his — I shove with Q waveclear and poke, but I will not all-in a Garen who can W away the burst and silence my follow-up. Level 6 gets me closest: if I land E and chain Pop Blossom's stun that is a real kill threat, and while I am disguised the preparation is hidden, so he never sees it coming. The catch is honest — Courage gives tenacity that shortens my stun, and his missing-HP true-damage R can out-trade me if my combo doesn't kill outright. Bait the Q, bait the W on its 22s, then commit.

edits.before: Use W's clone + invisibility to bait his Q gap-close, then land E (Tangle-Barbs) from an angle he can't predict
edits.after: Send the W clone to bait his Q gap-close, then land E (Tangle-Barbs) from the angle he just turned away from

edits.before: Damage reduction on cast — your burst only lands full once it is down. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Courage is 22s at rank 1 and eats your whole rotation — step up in the window after he burns it, never before it.

edits.before: That’s Garen’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Decisive Strike silences your E and R cast — inside 300 range you have no kit.

edits.before: Track Garen’s Courage: Damage reduction on cast — your burst only lands full once it is down. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Courage: it cuts your burst and grants tenacity, 22s at rank 1. His combo opens with a Decisive Strike auto reset — the wind-up is the cue.

notes: Row 6 conflict: the packet chart says Neeko owns 2+ items, and my whys[6] and spikes[3] both argue that case (AoE plus Pop Blossom into a group beats a single-target bruiser). The mirror's audit instead lists row 6 as Garen 6/10 while claiming to match the packet — those two cannot both be true. I resolved row 6 to Neeko in both layers because that is what the packet and the existing why-text say, and because the pre-existing full/content split on that row had to be closed either way. If mirror-fix.js flips it back, the whys[6]/spikes[3] text on this page will then contradict the chart and needs a matching rewrite.
